action_summary: An incoming plan claimed 23 high-leverage organs sit unwired on main and that a declarative bus would wire them. The first half is true and was measured: 27 named modules import in 1.1 s and 24-27 of them are referenced zero times by either front door. The second half is false: only 3 of 28 can run a self_check, so a fail-closed bus admits 3 and refuses 25. Along the way the SyntaxErrors were confirmed as real (5 existed; one tree-authored module was repaired and now routes a spreadsheet instruction end to end, the other is left as found because its only referee has never been green), and the '7,488 of a 7,534 ceiling' figure was measured false at 7,653 lines with no such ceiling anywhere in the verifier or the workflows.

(2) Declaring the 23 wired: the bus shows 25 cannot prove themselves, so a declaration would be a claim about names. (3) Trusting the plan's LOC and syntax figures: both were measured and one is false.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: OSWorld 2.0's authors diagnose frontier failure as weak recovery and maintenance of hidden state. A computer-use agent's action is only as good as the invocation it can compose from what the environment declares. Round 7 measured that the composition was wrong for reasons the environment had already published: the same 20 programs yield 33 doors when their declarations are misread and 57 when they are read, with no new knowledge acquired. No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.
